analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: Momentum and the AI complex are under pressure, with AI capex and funding concerns back in focus going into US earnings season. 14% of SPX reports the coming week and 44% the week after. The author says the next move depends more on earnings confirmation than anything else.

Positioning is very low. Net exposure in the US long/short cohort is at its lowest level in 5 years. GS prime data shows the tech sector had its largest ever 1-week net selling in the dataset's history, and both net exposure and the long/short ratio are at 0th percentile.

The author reads the index sell-off as a 'close the gap' / 'misery loves company' move driven by fear of benchmark underperformance, not a material portfolio risk adjustment. SPX hit an all-time high last week.

Breadth is improving ('the revenge of everything else'). The market had been narrow: 10 names make up almost 40% of the index, and a small portion of the index was responsible for over half of SPX y/y EPS growth. 350 SPX companies were green last week and SPX ex-AI outperformed SPX by 475bps.
The outperformance option pitched the prior week (SPX ex-AI vs SPX) is already at breakeven with 3 months to go.

AI debt burden is described as not new news. A WSJ article on AI borrowing flooding debt markets is a year old. The author says the issuance is large but this environment should not be confused with an unknown unknown.
Credit is stressed: CCCs broke above 1000 spread to benchmark relative to the rest of HY, and CDX IG is flinching significantly more than the VIX 1-month future.

Fundamental long/short managers returned -2.7% on the week (alpha -1.1%), -2.8% on the month (alpha -1.6%), and +9.8% on the year (weighted average). The author thinks the YTD figure feels high relative to floor conversations.

US central long/short hedge fund net exposure fell by its largest weekly decline since liberation day (-3.2) and sits at the 0th percentile on 1y, 2y and 5y horizons. Gross exposure did not fall with it and remains at 213.9% (83rd percentile, 3y). Managers have 'gotten less long' but not 'gotten smaller'.

Asset managers were better sellers, with sell skews in tech and macro product and demand in financials. Hedge funds were net sellers of both macro (ETFs) and tech. Selling by both hedge funds and long-only investors puts pressure on megacaps.
Semiconductors are down 8 sessions in a row, the longest streak since 2006, and are close to oversold on RSI for only the second time in 4 years.

CTA questions have moved from equities to government bonds. TLT is up 7 sessions in a row. GS expects CTAs to be short about $164mm/bp DV01 globally, with a baseline forecast of +12mm DV01 to buy over 1 week and +65mm over 1 month.
Friday was the largest SPX put volume session of all time (dollar notional), with over $3.3 trillion of notional traded.

The 'GS panic' index started the week at a one handle and finished at 7.4, one of the sharpest rallies on record. The GS index desk's delta-adjusted VIX showed one of the largest sessions of VIX outperformance in 3 years.
Pre-market single stock options will begin trading Monday on 29 tickers, with the first session 7:30a-9:25a.
The 'AI winners' vs 'AI at risk' basket pair trade is flat on the year, after being up almost 100% from 1 Jan 2026 through June month-end.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is already very low and breadth is improving, with 350 SPX names green last week and SPX ex-AI outperforming by 475bps. AI debt is not new news, and the sell-off looks like a 'close the gap' move, not a material risk adjustment.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum and the AI complex are under pressure. CCC spreads broke above 1000, CDX IG is moving more than the VIX 1-month future, gross exposure is still high at 213.9%, and hedge funds and long-only investors are both selling megacaps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings failing to confirm the AI complex, since the author says the next move depends on earnings confirmation.
